newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon banks' deposits reach $17.8 bln in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon banks' deposits reach $17.8 bln in Sept.

text.p: Lebanon's commercial bank deposits rose to $17.8 billion at the end of September, up by about $11 billion since December 1992, said a study from the Lebanese Banks Association published on Thursday.

The study also said banks' net revenues averaged 5.3 percent and pre-tax net porfits averaged 1.13 percent of total assets at the end of 1995. That compares with averages of 3.15 percent and 0.9 percent, respectively, for European banks.
Banks' return on capital averaged 33.9 percent compared with 25 percent in the United States and 24 percent in England, said the association comprised of Lebanon's 82 commercial banks.
It said banks' total capital jumped more than sixfold to $900 million from $143 million between December 1992 and September 1996. It expected the rising trend to continue for the next several years.

"We think that the capitalisation efforts will continue over the next four years at the same rate and momentum. The (postwar) rebuilding project requires a continuous increase in banks' capital," the study said.

Billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri has headed three cabinets since late 1992 with a mandate to rebuild Lebanon from the 1975-90 civil war, improving international confidence in the country and attracting capital inflows.
Last month, Bank of Lebanon governor Riad Salameh said encouraging banks to increase their capital was one of the central bank's essential goals over the past few years.

Despite efforts over the past four years to develop financial intermediation by introducing new instruments and creating new financial institutions, banks remain virtually the sole intermediaries in the market, the association said.
Banks' loans to the economy totalled $14.5 billion, or some 80 percent of their deposits, by the end of September 1996, the the study said.
"They (banks) have lent the public sector in Lebanese pounds and through the mechanism of treasury bill subscriptions about $6.5 billion," it said.
"In practice, banks finance 61 percent of the state's total public debt, including external debt, and 71 percent of internal debt," it added.
